label: prop:beta-stability
title: Beta-stability line from the Skein binding Lagrangian
html:
Proposition. Beta-stability line from the Skein binding Lagrangian

The stable neutron number n^*(p) for each element is determined by extremizing the Skein binding Lagrangian over n at fixed p.

Proposition. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q. For a multi-nucleon Hopf link L = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} with A = Z + N, the beta-stable configuration satisfies \partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} / \partial n = 0. This gives the beta-stability line:

  p^*(A)
  = 
  \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)}

where a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C is the Coulomb coefficient from the crossing asymmetry, and a_A is the Pauli asymmetry coefficient.

Equivalently, for a given p, the stable mass number is the fixed point of:

  A^*(p) = p \left(2 + \frac{a_C}{2a_A} {A^*}^{2/3}\right)

and n^*(p) = A^*(p) - p.
